definitions.explanation: an unreasonable accusation or complaint made without proper basis, often to pick a fight or find fault

examples.japanese: それは{言|い}い{掛|が}かりだ。
{言|い}い{掛|が}かりをつけられて{困|こま}った。
examples.english: I was troubled by someone picking a fight with me.

examples.japanese: {酔|よ}っ{払|ぱら}いに{言|い}い{掛|が}かりをつけられた。
examples.english: A drunk person started an argument with me over nothing.

notes:
{言|い}い{掛|が}かり refers to an unreasonable or fabricated accusation, often made as a pretext to start a confrontation or find fault.

COMMON PATTERNS:
- {言|い}い{掛|が}かりをつける: to make a baseless accusation, to pick a fight
- {言|い}い{掛|が}かりをつけられる: to be falsely accused
- {言|い}い{掛|が}かりをつけてくる: to come at someone with unfounded complaints

USAGE:
Always implies the complaint has no legitimate basis — the accuser is either looking for trouble or making excuses. Common in situations involving {酔|よ}っ{払|ぱら}い (drunks), unreasonable customers, or bullying.

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {因縁|いんねん}をつける: to pick a quarrel (more intimidating)
- {難癖|なんくせ}をつける: to find fault, nitpick (persistent criticism)
- {八|や}つ{当|あ}たりする: to take frustrations out on someone

cross_references.label: to take frustrations out on someone
